metadata.title: Complex Cobordism vs Representing Formal Group Laws

extraction_notes.note: One sentence both states the Borel-Serre result (external) and derives the paper's equivalence modulo torsion; it cannot be split, so it is one paper claim with Borel-Serre as its assumption.
Two examples exist only as figure captions with xypic diagrams; the caption text is the statement.
Proofs are prose paragraphs preceding the lemma/claim they justify; start and end chosen by reading.

metadata.extraction_comment: Informal note: most lemmas are justified by sketchy geometric/homotopical arguments in running text, and the main theorem is introduced by 'We therefore claim'.

nodes.statement: Milnor showed that the cohomology ring MU was naturally isomorphic to Lazard's ring Lambda, while Landweber and Novikov show the stronger result that the Hopf algebra (MU^*MU,MU^*) naturally represents Lazard's Hopf algebra.

nodes.statement: It may be worth remarking that the principal tools in the preceding are: the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence collapses for an even-concentrated cohomology theory over an even-concentrated space; and the ordinary cohomology of CP is the ordinary polynomial ring Z[x]; this feature it shares with the homology of the odd-sphere loopspaces Omega S^2n+1; indeed the Hopf Algebras H^*(CP) and H_*(OmegaS^2n+1) are isomorphic, which means it's hard to see (except that otimes is plainly special) why one should prefer cohomology for FGL purposes.

nodes.statement: In any category with products, for any pointed object * to X and any k:N there is a commuting k-cube of coordinate planes: the cube of pullbacks of k inclusions X^k-1 to X^k which themselves are the fibers at *to X of the k defining structure maps X^k to X.
nodes.raw_latex:
In any category with products, for any pointed object $* \to X$ and any $k:\mathbb{N}$ there is a commuting $k$-cube of coordinate planes: the cube of pullbacks of $k$ inclusions
$$ X^{k-1} \to X^k $$ 
which themselves are the fibers {\em at} $*\to X$ of the $k$ defining structure maps $X^k \to X$.

nodes.statement: A result that should be well-known due to Borel+Serre that in ordinary cohomology, H^*(B U(k),Z) to H^*(CP^times k;Z) is exactly the inclusion of the k!-invariants; it will follow from this, since we have an explicit-enough factorization of the maps CP^wedge k to rlaprule1pt0ptrule[.6ex].6em.4ptTh(B k!,CP^wedge k) to MU(k), and from the multiplicative underpinning of the Thom isomorphism, that our map L_2k to MU(k) is an equivalence modulo torsion.
nodes.raw_latex:
A result that should be well-known due to Borel+Serre \cite{borSer} that in ordinary cohomology, $H^*(\mathbf{B} U(k),\mathbb{Z}) \to H^*(\mathbb{CP}^{\times k};\mathbb{Z})$ is {\em exactly} the inclusion of the $k!$-invariants; it will follow from this, since we have an explicit-enough factorization of the maps
$$ \mathbb{CP}^{\wedge k} \to \rlap{\rule{1pt}{0pt}\rule[.6ex]{.6em}{.4pt}}\mathrm{Th}(\mathbf{B} k!,\mathbb{CP}^{\wedge k}) \to MU(k), $$
and from the multiplicative underpinning of the Thom isomorphism, that our map $L_{2k} \to MU(k)$ is an equivalence {\em modulo torsion}.

nodes.statement: Here, Gamma is the category of partial maps of finite sets; the degree of such an Abelian functor is defined there in terms of the joint kernels of forgetting: a functor T is of degree at-most d whenever, for all d-part partitions X = coprod_j X_j, the natural maps T(X) to bigoplus_i T(coprod_jneq i X_j) are all injective.
nodes.raw_latex:
Here, $\Gamma$ is the category of {\em partial} maps of finite sets; the {\em degree} of such an Abelian functor is defined there in terms of the joint kernels of forgetting: a functor $T$ is of degree at-most $d$ whenever, for all $d$-part partitions $X = \coprod_j X_j$, the natural maps
$$ T(X) \to \bigoplus_i T(\coprod_{j\neq i} X_j) $$ 
are all injective.
